1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die

podcast.body: Released in 1975, this album featured artwork depicting all four band members in leather jackets at a hamburger stand. This visual proved pivotal as it inspired fan Legs McNeill to rename his fanzine "Punk," thereby directly linking the band's image to the emerging genre. "The album that featured a picture of all four members in leather jackets, which inspired fan Legs McNeil to call his fan scene about this music, punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The artwork for this album, featuring the band and their friends inside a White Castle hamburger stand, all wearing old-style leather motorcycle jackets, inspired Legs McNeil and his buddy when they were deciding on a name for their fanzine. The band's appearance, described as looking like "wise guy punks from the 1950s" akin to Fonzy or Marlon Brando in "The Wild One," led directly to the fanzine being called "Punk." "And the artwork contains a shot of the band and their buddies inside a white castle hamburger stand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

podcast.body: This album features a famous picture inside its CD booklet that shows the band at a White Castle hamburger stand, wearing black leather jackets. This image, reminiscent of 1950s troublemakers like Marlon Brando and James Dean, inspired the authors of "Punk" fanzine to adopt the title, thereby linking the band to the very origin of the term "punk rock" for a new form of music. "This was on the inside of their 1975 album Go Girl Crazy. It's a shot of them at a white castle hamburger stand wearing black leather jackets."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
